title: How was your weekend? — and the door to A2
title_target: Как прошли выходные? — Kak proshli vykhodnye?
goal: Tell the story of your weekend in flowing sentences, and open the door to the biggest thing waiting at A2: pairs of perfective and imperfective verbs.
bekal: tell a sequence of past events
recognize aspect pairs: делал vs. сделал

dialogs.title: Диалог — Monday morning, end of the semester
dialogs.intro: Six months have passed since Unit 1. Ani and Марко talk fluently now. Notice the verbs that come in pairs: one for the process, one for the result.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: Good! On Saturday I spent all day writing an essay.
lines.literal: good! on — Saturday — I — whole — day — wrote (f, process) — essay.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: I did! On Sunday at two in the morning.
lines.literal: wrote-it-through! on — Sunday — at — two — hours — of-night.

lines.speaker: Марко:
lines.id: Congratulations! I spent all Sunday cooking.
lines.literal: I-congratulate! and — I — on — Sunday — cooked (process) — whole — day.

lines.speaker: Марко:
lines.id: Lasagna. Three hours. Then we ate it in twenty minutes.
lines.literal: lasagna. three — hours. then — ate-up — in — twenty — minutes.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: Classic. By the way, do you remember how we met?
lines.literal: classic. by-the-way, you — remember, how — we — met?

lines.speaker: Марко:
lines.id: Of course. You didn't speak any Russian at all.
lines.literal: of-course. you — not — spoke — in-Russian — at-all.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: And now we've been talking for twenty minutes and I understand everything.
lines.literal: and — now — we — talk — twenty — minutes — and — I — all — understand.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: Not bad. Well then, shall we go to class?

notes: **Almost every Russian verb lives in a pair.** One for the **process** (imperfective), one for the **finished result** (perfective). писать / написать, готовить / приготовить, читать / прочитать. ⚠️ English shows this difference with tenses ("was writing," "have written") or not at all; Russian forces it into the verb itself, every single time.

**Rule of thumb at A1: use the imperfective when there's a word of duration, the perfective when there's a result.** *Я **писала** эссе весь день* (I was writing all day — the process). *Я **написала** эссе* (the essay is done — the result). Words like *весь день*, *часто*, *обычно*, *долго* almost always call for the imperfective.

**Perfective verbs have no present tense.** It makes sense once you think about it: something finished can't be in progress. So *напишу* means "I **will** write it (to the end)," not "I'm writing." This is the second way to express the future that Unit 14 mentioned in passing.

**Perfectives are usually formed with a prefix.** писать → **на**писать, читать → **про**читать, делать → **с**делать, готовить → **при**готовить, есть → **съ**есть. The prefix can't be guessed and must be learned with its partner. Some pairs change in the middle instead: покупать / **купить**, говорить / **сказать**.

**Встретились is the past of встретиться (to meet) — a -ся verb from Unit 12, in its perfective form.** Notice that -ся still sticks on at the very end, after the past ending: встретил**ся**, встретила**сь**, встретили**сь**.
**Поздравляю means "congratulations" for an achievement.** The full form is *Поздравляю с …* + instrumental: *с днём рождения* (happy birthday), *с Новым годом* (happy New Year).
**Пойдём means "let's go" — the perfective of идти in the "we" form.** One of the most common ways to suggest something. Its partners: *Пошли!* (come on, more casual), *Давай пойдём* (let's go).

grammars.title: The most common aspect pairs
body: Learn them in pairs, not one at a time. Left column for processes and habits; right column for finished results.
after: ⚠️ The last two rows don't use a prefix but a completely different word. There are a few pairs like this, and all of them are very common — learn them as exceptions.

**How to choose in three seconds:** ask yourself whether your sentence is about *what went on for a while* (imperfective) or *what finally got done* (perfective). If you're still unsure at A1, use the imperfective — it's right more often, and the mistake is smaller.

grammars.title: Building a flowing story
body: Connectors that turn a list of events into a story.
after: Full example: *В субботу я **сначала** работала, **потом** гуляла в парке. **Вдруг** пошёл дождь, **поэтому** я поехала домой. **К счастью**, у меня был зонт.*
Translation: *On Saturday I first worked, then went for a walk in the park. Suddenly it started raining, so I went home. Fortunately, I had an umbrella.*

blocks.text: Beginners are often good at starting conversations and awkward at ending them. These phrases close them smoothly.

blocks.title: Six months — and what now
items: **If you've worked through these twenty units seriously, you now have roughly three hundred active words** — enough for almost all everyday business, because the first three hundred words cover more than half of what people actually say in ordinary conversation.

**What you don't have yet is speed.** That doesn't come from a book, and it won't come from a second book either. It comes from hours of listening and speaking. From now on, reading material and conversation partners are more useful than any course book.
**The most useful sentence in this whole course is:** *Извините, я не понимаю. Повторите, пожалуйста, помедленнее.* As long as you can say it, you'll never be truly stuck.
**Спасибо, и удачи!** — Thank you, and good luck.

exercises.prompt: Choose the right form — process or finished. The options are in parentheses.
items: Я весь день ____ (писать or написать) эссе.
Она ____ (готовить or приготовить) ужин, и мы поели.
Я ____ (читать or прочитать) эту книгу два раза.
Я ____ (читать or прочитать) книгу вчера вечером.

exercises.prompt: Write the perfective partner of each verb.
Put the words in the right order.

items: On Saturday I spent all day writing an essay.

answers: писала — написала — готовил — приготовила — читал — прочитал
сделать — посмотреть — купить — выпить — сказать — выучить
Как прошли выходные? — Я весь день писала эссе. — Вдруг пошёл дождь. — Мне пора. — Приятно было поговорить.
Как прошли выходные? — В субботу я весь день писала эссе. — И наконец написала. — Вдруг пошёл дождь. — Мне пора. — Увидимся, удачи!
wave: Reread Unit 1 now, before you close this book. The dialogue that felt impossible six months ago will now take you thirty seconds — and that's the most honest measure of your progress.
